segments.text: Why does a website load fast in Tokyo, and just as fast in Paris?
Your site lives on one origin server. If that server is far away, every request must travel thousands of miles, and back. That delay is called latency.
From Tokyo to a server in Virginia, one round trip takes around two hundred milliseconds. And a single page needs dozens of them.
A C D N fixes this. It places edge servers close to your users, each one holding copies of your files.
First visit? That is a cache miss. The edge asks the origin once, then keeps a copy.
Next visit? That is a cache hit. The edge already has the file, and answers right away.
Now a million visitors can share one copy, and the origin barely notices.
The result: pages load in milliseconds, and the origin handles far less traffic. Everyone gets the fast version.
A CDN. Content, closer to everyone.
